name: AND rule
summary: The AND gate built from H-boxes equals the AND gate built from triangles.
description:
The left-hand side is the standard ZH construction of the AND gate: an arity-3 H-box followed by an arity-2 H-box (Hadamard), which maps $|x,y\rangle$ to $2\,|x\wedge y\rangle$. The right-hand side is the way the AND gate is built in the ZX-calculus with *triangles*: each triangle maps $|0\rangle\mapsto|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle\mapsto|0\rangle+|1\rangle$ (in the orientation used here, up to a scalar), and the Z-spiders with a $\pi$ phase are the 'negate' spiders of the phase-free paper.

In the ZH-calculus the triangle is not a generator. Following the phase-free paper, each triangle is drawn here by its definition: a NOT followed by an arity-3 H-box with one leg plugged by a phase-free Z-state. This rule was added to the phase-free ZH-calculus to make it complete for the Toffoli-Hadamard fragment; it was later shown to be unnecessary in the rule set of the 2021 completeness paper.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers. The triangles are drawn expanded according to definition (Δ) of the phase-free paper.
